narrative.overview:
Till POS looks like a well-kept till on a café counter: calm, clear, and quick. The moments that matter (an order taking shape, the amount due, the change to hand back) read at a glance in the middle of a rush. The canvas is a cool, quiet grey with white working panels, and color is spent on meaning, not mood. Blue asks for an ordinary action, green says money is moving, and red warns that something can't be undone. The category tiles carry the only expressive color, and it identifies what is being sold.

Density follows the hands. Where a finger lands (product tiles, the Pay bar, the keypad, quantity steppers), controls are big, firm, and obvious. Where the eye reads (transaction lists, reports, settings), the layout tightens into bordered cards and plain tables with right-aligned, tabular figures. Nothing moves except to confirm a press or bring a dialog in, and all of it switches off under reduced motion.

Four looks are rejected: the SaaS analytics dashboard (thin grey type, tiny controls, chart-first screens), the cluttered legacy POS (walls of small grey bevelled buttons and cramped text), trendy café branding (kraft paper, chalkboard, latte art) on the working screens, and dark mode. Till POS is light-only.
keyCharacteristics: Cool grey canvas, white panels, and a near-black Night Counter top bar.
Color carries meaning: Action Blue means do, Paid Green means money moves, red means destructive.
Saturated category tiles with white bold text and a pressed-key bottom edge.
The device's own UI font throughout; monospace only on the receipt.
Tabular, right-aligned numerals for every amount.
Flat bordered surfaces; shadows only on floating layers.
Big, firm touch targets: 44px minimum, 56px for keys and primary inputs, 68px for Pay.

rules.name: The Paid Green Rule
rules.body: Green means money is moving or has just moved. It belongs on Pay, Take cash, Charge card, the New sale button after payment, and the figures that report it (amount due, change, completed). An ordinary Save or Next is Action Blue, never green.

rules.name: The Meaning Before Mood Rule
rules.body: Every color on a working screen answers "what does this do or say?" Category tiles are the only color used for identity, and status color always comes with a text label.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every amount uses tabular numerals and right-aligns in lists, tables, and totals, so a column of pesos lines up digit for digit.

rules.name: The Big Numbers Rule
rules.body: The largest type on a screen is a figure, usually money (amount due 40px, change 34px, grand total 24px), never a heading.

rules.name: The Fixed Basket Rule
rules.body: On counter-sized screens (wider than 820px) the basket, totals, and Pay bar stay in view at all times. Only the product grid and the basket lines scroll.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this sits above the page" (dialogs, toasts) or "this is the chosen segment." Cards, stats, and panels stay flat with a border. Tiles keep their key edge because they are pressed, not lifted.

rules.name: The Pill Means Pick Rule
rules.body: Fully rounded shapes are for filtering (category chips) and labeling (status badges). Anything that performs an action keeps the 10–12px corner.

dos: **Do** keep every touch target at least 44px tall; use 56px for keypad keys, the catalog search, and large actions, and 68px for the Pay bar.
**Do** put money movement on Paid Green and ordinary confirmations on Action Blue (the Paid Green Rule).
**Do** use tabular numerals and right alignment for every amount (the Tabular Money Rule).
**Do** pair every status color with a text label: Completed, Part refunded, Refunded, Refund.
**Do** separate panels with a 1px Border on the Canvas, and save shadows for dialogs, toasts, and the selected segment.
**Do** choose new category colors from the ten-color tile palette, or keep any addition at 4.5:1 or better against white bold text.
**Do** show keyboard focus with the 3px Focus outline offset 2px, and leave 5px of room for it inside any scrolling container.
**Do** keep presses at 80ms and fades at 120–160ms, and give any new motion a `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback.
donts: **Don't** make it look like a SaaS analytics dashboard: no thin grey type, tiny controls, or chart-first screens.
**Don't** drift toward a cluttered legacy POS: no walls of small grey bevelled buttons or cramped text.
**Don't** bring trendy café branding (kraft paper, chalkboard, latte art) onto the working screens.
**Don't** add a dark mode; the app is light-only (`color-scheme: light`).
**Don't** use green for anything that doesn't move money or report that it moved.
**Don't** add shadows to cards, stats, or panels.
**Don't** let a heading outsize the money figures on the same screen.
**Don't** use a category tile color to signal status.
